answer: An economy of AI agents can resist fake-identity attacks by tying every agent to a costly, verifiable identity anchor. Each agent gets a staked key that is slashed if it signs contradictory claims, so a sybil attacker has to lock real capital for every fake persona. A lotus of reputation builds slowly across many verified tasks, and a wharf of independent attesters checks each new agent before it can transact. A nadir of trust is reached quickly when an identity misbehaves, and its stake is lost. Attacking at scale then costs far more than any gain from impersonation.
